h: True Holiness Remains Humble and Seeks Counsel

p: when they saw the new fire,
they rose to add love upon love;
'and they took' — 'taking' means nothing but joy."
That it expounds this as an expression of joy
there is no joy like it,"
and if the opposite, then the opposite;
for them there was complete joy,
and this is why it says "vayehi,"
while for the nations of the world it was "vai," woe.
And so it is in all of them:
for the righteous, "and there was light"
and for the wicked, from whom the light was withheld,
So too it expounds the expression "vayikchu":
for it was not a complete joy;
that they had already been perfected,
since they merited to see a new fire,
a renewed light, as in the future,
"And a new spirit I will put within you";
and they merited to straighten the heart,
But the joy was not complete,
for on that very day they died.
"Why does the verse say 'the sons of Aharon'?
For they did not accord honor to Aharon."
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בְּתוֹרַת כֹּהֲנִים
based on what they said in Toras Kohanim
'Now your sons are found to be
for through them the House was sanctified.'
צִדֵּק עָלָיו אֶת הַדִּין וְשָׁתַק כוּ׳
he accepted the judgment as just and was silent, etc.;
to accept the judgment upon themselves as just.
Avraham accepted the judgment upon himself,
Yaakov accepted the judgment upon himself,
'I am too small for all the kindnesses, etc.'"
And this has no explanation at all:
for regarding Aharon, who was punished,
that he accepted the judgment upon himself;
where we find no punishment at all,
And its explanation appears to be
would I not have been dust?
would I not have been ashes?"
it was settled in his mind
to be burned in Ur Kasdim,
even though he gave himself up
for the sanctification of the Name of Heaven;
and likewise had he been killed
in the war of the kings,
even though he was zealous for the Name of Hashem,
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ מִדְרַשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא לֶךְ לְךָ ז)
(as stated in Midrash Tanchuma, Lech Lecha 7).
And this is what it says:
as it says, 'And I am dust and ashes'";
that is, he justified upon himself
and said that only by Hashem's kindness did he escape.
And likewise Yaakov Avinu, alav hashalom,
although he was like Adam HaRishon
and knew nothing of evil at all,
and was worthy of all miracles,
he accepted the judgment upon himself,
אִם הָיָה נֶהֱרָג עַל יְדֵי לָבָן וְעֵשָׂו
had he been killed by Lavan and Esav;
he said that it was by Hashem's kindness:
"I am too small for all the kindnesses, etc."
even though he had already been perfected with every perfection,
as they said in Toras Kohanim (above, 17):
and merited the lifting of the hands (Birkas Kohanim)
for himself and for his generations
show that his body is holy,
for he eats of the sacred things of Heaven;
and these kohanim are the agents of the Merciful One,
And likewise the redemption of the firstborn:
"And the firstborn of your sons you shall redeem";
and he gives the redemption to the kohen,
who is the agent of the Merciful One.
And the lifting of the hands
"And they went out and blessed the people,
וַיֵּרָא כְבוֹד ה׳ אֶל כָּל הָעָם
and the glory of Hashem appeared to all the people";
and they merited to see a new fire.
and justified the judgment of Heaven upon himself,
Such a sin is in my hand and in the hand of my sons,
that I have come to this."
And likewise with the anointing oil,
even though Moshe made it at the word of the Almighty,
"Woe is me, for I have misappropriated the anointing oil,"
as they said in Toras Kohanim (37).
since they merited to see a new fire
and saw that they had been perfected,
sought to add love upon love,
and did not suspect themselves of being mistaken,
and that perhaps they had not been perfected.
And in this they did not accord honor to Aharon,
to say: "Our father is surely good and perfected,
he suspects himself of being a sinner and a misappropriator,
And this is the main thing:
that he has nothing before his Creator;
that he has been fully perfected,
lest there be an error in his hand.
And this is along the lines of what they said
that sufferings are coming upon him,
let him examine his deeds, etc.;
if he did not find anything,
let him attribute it to neglect of Torah."
And this is what it says, "because of my folly,"
that is, through neglect of Torah:
even though he found no sin in his hand,
he accepted the judgment upon himself.
And this is the main thing:
that a person always inquire and seek,
and "this is the whole of man" (Koheles 12:13).
And let him not rely on his own opinion;
And this is what it expounds afterward:
"They did not take counsel from Moshe,
and they did not take counsel from one another."
וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהָיוּ גְּדוֹלִים וּשְׁלֵמִים
And even though they were great and perfect,
that they relied on their own opinion and on their own holiness.
that a person should not rely on his own understanding;
and even when he knows in his soul
that he is a perfect tzaddik,
and seek the words of Torah

inlineHeadings.text: The Avos Receive Everything as Kindness
Aharon Remains Humble in His Holiness
Examining Oneself and Seeking Wise Counsel
